title: Canonical invocation delivery
summary: Every delegated stage MUST receive the complete canonical invocation contract, unshadowed by the supervisor and auditable after the fact.
instructions: Delivery MUST achieve three outcomes: the worker holds the complete canonical contract, the supervisor adds no parallel contract, and the delivered body stays auditable.

Harness-spawned external execution is a permitted delivery mechanism: for a stage whose persona resolves to an external executor, the harness delivers the canonical card to the spawned process and MUST author the delegation artifact itself. Supervisor delivery rules below bind only cursor-executor stages; the external path MUST follow EXECUTOR-001.

For a cursor-executor stage, the supervisor MUST launch the named projected agent the card’s delegation block points at (the `.cursor/agents/pan-<persona>.md` definition, including any run-scoped variant the path names) and MUST do so from the top level of the agent hierarchy. Experimentally confirmed 2026-08-18: Cursor honors the definition’s model mapping only at top level — any spawn made from inside another subagent ALWAYS runs the platform default model — and a worker’s self-reported model string is not evidence of what launched. Ad-hoc subagents remain valid for auxiliary work that is not a stage delegation, such as repository exploration or debugging, within the two-level nesting cap DELEGATE-001 defines.

The top-level requirement applies transitively to command templates, agent-slash resolution, and resume paths. A projected surface MUST NOT instruct a session to delegate a workflow supervisor to a child agent. Validation MUST reject a command template that does.
The supervisor SHOULD record the launched agent name as the single label line the delegation validator permits ahead of the delivered body, so a wrong launch route stays auditable.
Before delegation, the supervisor MUST use the harness-produced invocation validation artifact and MUST NOT delegate a card whose validation status is failed or missing.

When the invocation declares `referenced` delivery, the supervisor MUST deliver the generated delivery prompt exactly as rendered. The prompt names the canonical contract path, its digest, and its complete section index.
When the invocation declares `verbatim` delivery, the supervisor MUST paste the complete canonical invocation Markdown into the subagent prompt.
Under either mode the supervisor MUST NOT summarize, narrow, reorder, or restate the contract, and MUST NOT deliver a path-only reference that carries no digest and no section index.

The supervisor MUST persist the exact delivered prompt body to the matching `<invocation-id>.delegation.md` artifact that the card resolves, before stage submission, so the harness can validate delivery.

The supervisor MUST NOT append parallel scope, policy, gate, or plan restatements that could shadow the canonical contract; a minimal non-conflicting persona label MAY precede it. The supported label is one `Agent: <launched agent name>` line followed by one blank line.
A worker that receives a referenced contract MUST read the complete contract before other repository context, and MUST declare that read in `invocation_attestation` in its stage output.

A read attestation MUST name the invocation, the contract path, the contract digest, and every contract section in order with its digest. A partial, reordered, or stale attestation MUST fail the stage.
A worker that cannot read the referenced contract MUST report stage result `blocked` with attestation status `reference_failed` and the concrete read error. It MUST NOT report a product verdict.
A missing or mismatched delegation artifact MUST be repaired against the same active invocation rather than bypassed or represented as successful delivery.
